home.slogan: Thoughtful furniture and lighting for spaces that feel good to live in. Designed in Ljubljana, made by small European workshops, and delivered across the EU.

workingHours.note: For personal consultations, material reviews, or collection of larger orders, we recommend booking an appointment in advance. The showroom may be closed on public holidays and during our annual studio break.

about.text: NORD Atelier is an independent design studio and online shop for furniture, lighting, and considered home objects. We combine a calm northern aesthetic with local craft knowledge and materials selected for a long service life. Every piece is developed to be comfortable to use, easy to maintain, and distinctive enough to give a room its own identity.

items.text: We select materials according to origin, tactile quality, and repairability. Our core palette includes certified solid wood, powder-coated metal, natural oils, wool, and recycled glass. We visit suppliers in person and develop production details with them to reduce waste at every stage.

Our collections are conceived as adaptable systems rather than short-lived trends. Tables, shelving, and seating can be extended, reupholstered, or adjusted for a new room. This allows each piece to remain useful as homes, teams, and everyday needs evolve.

Alongside online purchasing, we offer guidance on dimensions, colours, and material combinations. For larger orders we prepare layouts, samples, and a coordinated delivery and installation plan, making the path from first idea to finished room clear and predictable.

team.text: Our small interdisciplinary team carries each design idea through prototyping, production, the online experience, and final installation. We stay directly involved in every project, keeping decisions fast, communication transparent, and the outcome consistent from the first sketch to the final detail.

items.name: Ana Kovač
items.text: Founder and creative director leading collection development and interior projects. Her work focuses on the relationship between light, natural materials, and the everyday habits of the people using a space.

items.name: Luka Zupan
items.text: Product designer responsible for construction details, prototypes, and collaboration with makers. He looks for a balance between simple assembly, efficient material use, and long-term comfort.

items.name: Maja Vidmar
items.text: Architect and project lead coordinating surveys, drawings, samples, schedules, and on-site delivery. She helps clients turn broad ambitions into a clear set of decisions and a workable budget.

items.name: Nejc Potočnik
items.text: E-commerce and support lead responsible for product data, orders, delivery, and aftercare. His goal is to make even complex online purchases clear, informed, and free from unpleasant surprises.

experience.text: Over the past years we have furnished private homes, boutique hotels, restaurants, offices, and shops across Slovenia and neighbouring countries. Lessons from project work feed directly into product development, so our collections are tested in real spaces and under demanding everyday use.

reviews.text: Clients most often recommend us for a clear process, calm communication, and solutions that are visually distinctive without sacrificing practicality. The comments below reflect different kinds of collaboration, from a single online purchase to a complete interior fit-out.

items.title: Thoughtful from first sketch to installation
items.text: The team turned our loose list of wishes into a warm, functional home. Material choices were clearly explained, the schedule was realistic, and installation was exceptionally organised. Two years later, the furniture still looks excellent and works without compromise.

items.title: An online purchase with a personal touch
items.text: Before ordering our dining chairs, we received fabric samples and a precise explanation of the available versions. Delivery was announced in advance, packaging was considered, and instructions were clear. That level of support makes a substantial remote purchase much easier.

items.title: A distinctive identity for our boutique hotel
items.text: NORD connected the reception, breakfast room, and guest rooms into one coherent story without making them feel identical. We especially value the durable materials, replaceable parts, and documentation that helps our staff maintain everything properly.

items.title: A reliable partner for a demanding store opening
items.text: Despite a tight deadline, drawings, samples, and deliveries remained transparent throughout. The team resolved on-site changes quickly and suggested details that improved visitor flow. The space opened on time without lowering the quality of the final result.

portfolio.text: Project work allows us to explore scale, materials, and user habits across very different settings. This selection includes private interiors, hospitality spaces, retail environments, and product collections, showing how the same design principles adapt to different clients and budgets.

items.title: Apartment by the Ljubljanica
items.text: This city apartment renovation opened the central living area and introduced a continuous furniture line connecting the kitchen, library, and workspace. Oak, linen, and brushed steel form a calm foundation, while movable lighting and coloured accents let the room adapt throughout the day.

items.title: House beneath Storžič
items.text: For this family house we developed a durable interior able to handle wet hiking gear, children, and frequent gatherings. Built-in storage contains everyday clutter while the central table remains an open meeting point. Local larch gains character over time and connects the rooms with the surrounding landscape.

items.title: Hotel Mura lounge
items.text: The public area of this boutique hotel was planned as a sequence of smaller, comfortable zones for breakfast, work, and evening conversation. Custom banquettes reduce noise, while layered lighting creates an inviting atmosphere from early morning until late at night.

items.title: Kora bakery
items.text: This compact bakery is organised around a clear route from entrance to display and collection. Warm timber and textured tiles reinforce the handmade character, while modular shelving supports frequent changes in the offer. High-wear components can be replaced without major construction work.

items.title: Axis collection
items.text: Axis is a family of tables, benches, and shelves built around a single aluminium joint. The system supports multiple lengths and heights, allowing it to work in a small apartment, office, or hospitality setting. Individual components can be ordered separately and replaced with simple tools.

items.title: Lightwell installation
items.text: For the entrance lobby of an office building, we developed a composition of hand-blown glass lights responding to the height of the space and the view from the street. Warm light reveals the glass texture, while controls adapt intensity to daylight and evening events.

services.text: Our services are modular: you can choose a focused consultation, development of a single custom piece, or a complete process from concept to installation. Scope, timing, and deliverables are defined at the start, making shared decisions and responsibilities clear at every stage.

items.title: Interior concept and space planning
items.text: For homes, hospitality venues, and smaller workplaces, we prepare a functional layout, material direction, and selection of key pieces. The process includes an analysis of user habits, several planning options, and clear visual material so decisions can be made confidently before ordering.

items.title: Custom furniture development
items.text: When standard dimensions or functions are not enough, we develop furniture around the room and the way it will be used. We prepare construction details, samples, and prototypes of critical parts, then coordinate manufacturing with the selected workshop and monitor quality through installation.
features: Site survey and verification of existing conditions
Coordination of production, delivery, and installation

items.title: Lighting, textile, and material curation
items.text: An existing room can improve dramatically without construction work. By combining general, task, and ambient lighting with carefully selected textiles, we create better comfort, acoustics, and atmosphere. Recommended products can be ordered directly through the atelier.
features: Review of existing lighting and practical needs
Plan for lighting layers and colour temperatures
Selection of curtains, rugs, and upholstery
Samples and comparison across price levels

items.title: Delivery, installation, and final styling
items.text: For larger orders we prepare a single logistics plan, verify access and surface protection, and coordinate the arrival of different makers. After installation we complete a quality check, remove packaging, and position smaller elements so the space is ready for immediate use.

blog.text: Our journal shares practical lessons from projects, material explainers, and a look into product development. The articles are written for anyone who wants to make more considered decisions about space, quality, and the long-term use of furniture.

items.title: How to choose a dining table for everyday life
items.description: A good dining table needs to account for more than the number of chairs. We explain useful clearances, the differences between shapes, how bases affect comfort, and which materials can handle remote work, children’s projects, and long dinners.
items.author: Ana Kovač

items.title: Three layers of light for a more comfortable home
items.description: A single ceiling light rarely supports every activity. Using a practical example, we show how to combine general, task, and ambient lighting, choose an appropriate colour temperature, and reduce glare during the evening.
items.author: Maja Vidmar

items.title: Solid wood, veneer, or laminate: what should you choose
items.description: Each material has a sensible place. We compare feel, cost, durability, repair options, and common maintenance mistakes so you can choose according to the room and level of use rather than appearance alone.
items.author: Luka Zupan

items.title: What happens between ordering and furniture delivery
items.description: Making a quality piece involves material procurement, workshop drawings, production, finishing, and quality control. We outline a typical process and explain why lead times differ between standard and customised products.
items.author: Nejc Potočnik

items.title: A small space without small ambitions
items.description: Small apartments benefit most from clear priorities and furniture that performs more than one task. We share five tested approaches to storage, circulation, folding elements, and visual calm without making the room feel empty.
items.author: Ana Kovač

pricing.note: All prices include 22% VAT. Standard delivery within Slovenia is calculated at checkout; international delivery, installation, and customised products are quoted separately. Product photographs may differ slightly from the actual materials due to screen settings.

careers.text: We look for curious, reliable colleagues who understand that a good product is built through many precise decisions. We work in small project teams, share knowledge openly, and value the ability to communicate clearly with designers, makers, suppliers, and clients.

items.title: Product designer
items.text: We are looking for a designer with experience in furniture or related physical products. You will contribute to research, 3D modelling, technical details, prototypes, and the preparation of products for repeatable production.
requirements: At least three years of experience developing physical products.
Independent CAD work and the ability to prepare clear technical drawings.
Understanding of timber, metal, upholstery, or related production processes.
Fluent communication in Slovenian and English.
items.note: Full-time role based in Ljubljana with up to two remote days per week. Please include a portfolio, a short explanation of your role in the projects shown, and your approximate availability date.

items.title: E-commerce and content manager
items.text: We are looking for someone to own product data quality, the content calendar, online campaigns, and improvements to the purchase journey. The role combines analytics, writing, photography coordination, and daily collaboration with customer support.
requirements: Experience managing an online shop or digital product.
Excellent writing skills and a strong sense of information structure.
Basic understanding of analytics, SEO, and user-experience testing.
Ability to organise multiple products, languages, and deadlines at once.
items.note: The role can be full-time or structured as a four-day week. Please send an example of content or a shop where you were responsible for a measurable result.

items.title: Installer and technical coordinator
items.text: For deliveries and installations across Slovenia, we are looking for a technically skilled person who can calmly resolve unexpected site conditions. The work includes equipment preparation, access coordination, furniture assembly, and documenting the final inspection.
requirements: Experience with furniture installation, joinery, or comparable work.
Precision, respect for client spaces, and appropriate physical fitness.
Category B driving licence; C1 is an advantage.
Willingness to accommodate occasional early starts and multi-day installations.
items.note: We offer permanent employment, quality tools, fully covered travel expenses, and additional training for more complex systems. The start date is flexible by agreement.

faq.text: Below you will find answers to common questions about ordering, materials, delivery, and customisation. For a product or project requiring additional checks, send us dimensions, photographs of the room, and your preferred timing so we can provide a more precise answer.

items.question: Can I receive material samples before ordering?
items.answer: Yes. Small sample sets are available for most fabrics, timber finishes, and metal colours. The sample cost is deducted from a larger order. With natural timber and stone, remember that a single sample represents only part of the normal variation.

items.question: How long do production and delivery take?
items.answer: In-stock products normally ship within three to five working days. Standard made-to-order pieces take approximately six to ten weeks, while customised versions generally require ten to fourteen weeks. We confirm the exact schedule after reviewing the order and material availability.

items.question: Do you deliver outside Slovenia?
items.answer: Yes, we deliver to most European Union countries. Smaller items are shipped by parcel service, while furniture receives an individual quote based on the address, access, and installation requirements. Any limitations or additional costs are confirmed before payment.

items.question: Which products can be customised?
items.answer: Most tables, shelving, seating, and lighting are available in several dimensions, colours, or materials. Structural changes are reviewed separately because they can affect stability, price, and lead time. Before confirmation you receive a specification and, where necessary, a drawing.

items.question: How do returns of standard products work?
items.answer: An unused standard product can be returned within the statutory period when it remains in original condition and is properly protected for transport. Customised items, assembled pieces showing use, and opened samples are generally non-returnable. Always contact support before sending anything back.

items.question: Do you provide installation and packaging removal?
items.answer: Within Slovenia, most larger products can be delivered into the room, installed, and cleared of packaging. The service is priced according to location, access, floor level, and product complexity. Before arrival we verify the route dimensions and any need for floor protection or lifting equipment.

items.question: How should I care for timber and upholstered products?
items.answer: For timber, use a soft damp cloth, wipe spills promptly, and avoid aggressive cleaners. Vacuum upholstery regularly with a soft attachment and treat stains according to the selected fabric instructions. Detailed care guidance for your exact finish is supplied with delivery.

schedule.title: Showroom and event schedule
schedule.text: The showroom is open for independent visits and booked consultations. The schedules below show regular times for consultations, material workshops, and deliveries. Special events and holiday changes are published in the Events section.

items.title: Showroom consultations
items.text: For a larger purchase, book a 45- or 90-minute appointment. This allows us to prepare relevant samples, check dimensions in advance, and involve the team member whose expertise best matches your project.

cells: Longer project sessions and sample review

items.title: Material and care workshops
items.text: These short practical workshops compare materials, demonstrate correct care, and explain production methods. Places are limited because every participant works with samples and may bring a photograph or small item for an individual question.

cells: Timber finishes, stains, and minor repairs
Lighting, colour temperature, and fixture placement

items.title: Delivery, installation, and collection
items.text: Larger deliveries are scheduled in morning windows to leave enough time for installation and inspection. Personal collection is available only after confirmation because part of the stock is held at a separate logistics facility.

cells: A narrower window is confirmed the day before delivery
At least 5 working days in advance
Timing depends on the carrier and customs procedures

events.text: The atelier regularly hosts product launches, conversations with designers, and small practical workshops. Events are designed for limited groups, leaving enough time for questions, prototype viewing, and discussion of participants’ specific challenges.

items.title: From timber sample to the right finish
items.text:
This practical workshop compares oiled, lacquered, and soap-finished surfaces and shows how they respond to water, grease, and everyday cleaning.

Participants will prepare their own sample, receive care instructions, and may bring a photograph of an existing piece for a short individual recommendation.

items.title: Soft Geometry collection launch
items.text:
We will introduce a new seating series exploring soft transitions between supporting structure and upholstery. Finished pieces, early prototypes, and fabric samples will be on display.

The evening includes a short conversation with the design and production team followed by time for an informal viewing of the collection.

items.title: Lighting for the winter months
items.text:
Architect Maja Vidmar will use residential examples to show how to position light sources, reduce glare, and improve evening comfort without major alterations.

The talk is followed by a demonstration of different colour temperatures and an opportunity for a short consultation about your own room.
items.location: City Museum of Ljubljana, projection room

items.title: Furniture repair and reuse clinic
items.text:
This clinic covers basic diagnosis of loose joints, surface damage, and worn upholstery. We will demonstrate safe repairs suitable for home and explain when professional help is the better option.

The session has been cancelled due to the instructor’s illness; registered participants will receive priority when a new date is announced.

items.title: Open studio: prototypes and process
items.text:
Once a year we open the working studio and share development models, failed experiments, and decisions that normally remain hidden behind the finished product.

The visit is informal and suitable for students, clients, and anyone interested in how an idea becomes a useful object.
